result.title: Second-Order Dynamics in Noisy RNNs Produce Exploration and Temporal Compression in Replay
result.summary: Biological neural networks (like the hippocampus) can internally generate "replay" resembling stimulus-driven activity. Recent computational models of replay use noisy recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained to path-integrate. Replay in these networks is described as Langevin sampling, but this theory alone fails to capture the environmental exploration and temporal compression observed in real biological replay. To close this gap, we re-examine spontaneous noisy RNN activity ("replay") as Langevin sampling, one timestep at a time, from a time-series distribution resembling lived experiences (unlike previous works which defined sampling as Monte Carlo inference over a static distribution). We provide a normative second-order Langevin sampling framework wherein spike-frequency adaptation drives spatial exploration at the cost of speed, and momentum via dendritic input differentiation drives temporal compression. We numerically verify our framework via simulations of noisy RNNs trained on 2D triangular and T-maze navigation activity, and others trained on place cell activity of synthetic rats. Crucially, we observe that simultaneous adaptation and momentum increases both replay exploration and speed, and provide one of the first accounts for biologically plausible temporal compression in rate-based RNN replay. Our findings encourage experiments into whether dendritic input differentiation, or other mechanisms, may support temporal compression in memory circuits like the hippocampus.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文将噪声 RNN 中自发产生的「replay」重新解释为对时序经验分布逐时间步采样的第二阶 Langevin 过程，提出由 spike-frequency adaptation 驱动空间探索、由树突输入微分提供动量以产生时间压缩，并用三角迷宫、T 迷宫与合成大鼠位置细胞活动仿真加以验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「二阶状态更新—动量—时间压缩」框架可能与 LVR 中 latent 轨迹如何在探索充分性与长度压缩之间权衡相关，且对循环状态如何在内部推进推理提供概念类比，但属神经科学模型，需核查可迁移性。
